newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says Belarus might merge with Russia.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says Belarus might merge with Russia.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin told Russian media chiefs on Friday that Belarus might merge with Russia in future, Interfax news agency said.
"Maybe after all this will be a single state," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying.
Hardline Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko said however on Friday the former Soviet republic had no plans for a full-scale merger.

"Belarus will remain an independent state," spokesman Valery Tolkachyov quoted Lukashenko as saying in an interview with the British Broadcasting Corporation early on Friday, before Yeltsin's remarks were reported.
"There is nothing in Yeltsin's statement saying Russia and Belarus will become a single state in April or May," Tolkachyov said. "Today we are only talking about a union of two independent states."
Russia and Belarus have announced plans to seek closer integration but so far Moscow has been cautious about how far it might go.

Last April Russia and Belarus, a Slav country where a majority of the population backs closer integration, formed a tighter bilateral community inside the loose 12-member Commonwealth of Independent States.

But Moscow officials have so far made clear that a full merger can only be discussed after Belarus moves further than its current rudimentary stage of economic reform and improves its record on human rights and political freedom.
Critics in Moscow say Russia will have to bear the financial cost of the merger, an expense it can ill afford because of its own economic crisis and growing public discontent.
Belarus nationalist groups and even some officials fear the merger means huge Russia swallowing up its small neighbour.
"It is hard to say how integration will develop and the president also said today that it is hard to say what awaits us in the future," Lukashenko's spokesman said.
Yeltsin said he would meet the Belarussian president on April 2 to discuss further steps in integration between the two states.
"We should seriously advance in our relations and show an example for other Commonwealth states," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying.
